glosses: A specific pitch.
(in the diatonic scale) An interval of a major second.
(in a Gregorian chant) A recitational melody.
The character of a sound, especially the timbre of an instrument or voice.
The pitch of a word's sound that distinguishes a difference in meaning, as for example in Chinese.
A whining style of speaking; a kind of mournful or artificial strain of voice; an affected speaking with a measured rhythm and a regular rise and fall of the voice.

examples.text: Children often read with a tone.

glosses: The manner in which speech or writing is expressed, especially the aspects of diction (word choice), connotation, emotiveness, and register.

examples.text: Their tone was dissatisfied, almost menacing.

glosses: State of mind; temper; mood.

examples.text:

The strange situation I am in and the melancholy state of public affairs, […] drag the mind down […] from a philosophical tone or temper, to the drudgery of private and public business.

examples.text: We make crude visual distinctions and effectively meaningless categorizations based on average skin tones, such as black or white.

examples.text: This picture has tone.

glosses: The definition and firmness of a muscle or organ; see also: tonus.

examples.text: Her rousing speech gave an upbeat tone to the rest of the evening.

examples.text: "I am going to raise the tone of the business. That's wot I want you for. To raise the tone of the business."
